title: Veeda Raises $90M to Build Robot Training World Models
summary: The former Nvidia researchers aim to create simulated worlds where robots can learn safely through large-scale trial and error.
body:
## A virtual training ground for physical AI

Veeda AI has emerged from stealth with more than $90 million in seed financing to develop world models for robotics. The company is led by Sanja Fidler, formerly Nvidia’s vice president of AI research, alongside longtime collaborators Zan Gojcic and Huan Ling. Khosla Ventures and Radical Ventures are backing the startup.

Veeda’s proposed product is not a general-purpose robot or a conventional simulation package. It wants to build generative, multimodal models that can produce physically plausible virtual environments from sensor and real-world data. Robots would receive virtual bodies inside those environments, allowing their control systems to interact, make mistakes and improve without damaging equipment or endangering people.

The company argues that imitation learning from recorded human behavior will not be sufficient for broadly capable robots. Its alternative is interactive learning at scale: exposing machines to many variations of an environment and letting them test actions repeatedly. Veeda describes this simulated-reality layer as shared infrastructure that could support robot training and evaluation across manufacturing, logistics, transportation and other physical industries.

Fidler’s team brings experience spanning generative AI, computer vision, 3D reconstruction and robotics simulation. Veeda lists operations in Toronto, Mountain View, Zürich and Singapore, but has not yet disclosed a model, dataset, customer or release schedule. The financing therefore represents a substantial bet on the team and technical thesis rather than a demonstrated commercial system.

## Why it matters

Robotics is increasingly constrained by data rather than hardware alone. Real-world experiments are slow, costly and difficult to reproduce, while hand-built simulators struggle to match the variety and visual complexity of reality. If generative world models can provide sufficiently accurate physics, perception and interaction, they could become for robotics what large-scale training corpora became for language models. Veeda’s unusually large seed round makes it one of the best-funded new efforts to build that foundational layer, although its central claims remain to be validated in working systems.
title_zh: Veeda获超9000万美元融资，押注机器人世界模型
summary_zh: 这家由英伟达前研究负责人创办的公司，希望构建可大规模试错的模拟世界，让机器人以更安全、低成本的方式学习。
body_zh:
## 为机器人搭建虚拟训练场

Veeda AI 宣布结束隐身状态，并完成超过 9000 万美元种子轮融资，目标是研发面向机器人的世界模型。公司由英伟达前 AI 研究副总裁 Sanja Fidler 与长期合作者 Zan Gojcic、Huan Ling 共同创办，投资方包括 Khosla Ventures 和 Radical Ventures。

Veeda 要做的不是一款通用机器人，也不是传统的仿真软件。其核心设想是利用传感器和现实世界数据训练多模态生成模型，构建符合物理规律的虚拟环境。机器人可在其中获得“虚拟身体”，持续与环境交互、犯错并改进，无需承担损坏设备或危及人员的现实代价。

公司认为，仅靠模仿人类示范不足以训练出能力广泛的机器人。它选择的路线是规模化交互学习：为机器提供大量环境变化，让其反复尝试不同动作。Veeda 希望把这层“模拟现实”建设成通用基础设施，服务于制造、物流、交通等行业的机器人训练与评估。

创始团队的经验横跨生成式 AI、计算机视觉、三维重建和机器人仿真。Veeda 目前在多伦多、山景城、苏黎世和新加坡设有团队，但尚未公布具体模型、数据集、客户或发布时间表。因此，这笔融资首先是投资者对团队和技术路线的重注，而非对已经得到商业验证的产品追加投资。

## 为什么重要

机器人发展的瓶颈正从硬件扩展到训练数据。现实环境中的试验速度慢、成本高，也很难精确复现；人工搭建的仿真器则难以覆盖真实世界的复杂度和多样性。如果生成式世界模型能够同时提供足够可靠的物理规律、视觉感知和交互反馈，它可能像大规模语料之于语言模型一样，成为机器人能力扩张的基础。Veeda 罕见的大额种子轮融资，使其成为这一方向资金最充足的新进入者之一，但其关键技术主张仍需通过可运行系统验证。
